channel.title: WireShaman
channel.description: Cybersecurity and technology intelligence: what's actually breaking, how it works, and what to do about it.

item.title: What Is OAuth? Authorization, Tokens and PKCE Explained
item.dc:creator: WireShaman News Desk
item.description: OAuth lets an application receive limited access to another service without receiving the user's password. Here is how roles, tokens, scopes and PKCE fit together.

item.title: AMD's 192GB Ryzen AI Halo Pushes Local AI Beyond Laptop Memory Limits
item.dc:creator: WireShaman News Desk
item.description: AMD's new Ryzen AI Halo developer platform combines a Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 with up to 192GB of unified memory for large local AI workloads.

item.title: OnePlus 16 Launches in China: 3,840Hz “Oriental” LTPO Display, 200MP Camera, 9,000mAh Battery
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: OnePlus announced the OnePlus 16 in China on October 12, headlined by its 4th Gen Oriental display, Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, and 9,000mAh battery. What we know, what is confirmed, and what is still unverified.

item.title: CISA Warns of Active Zero-Day Exploits in Citrix NetScaler — New CVE Added
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: CISA expanded its Citrix NetScaler alert on October 9, adding CVE-2026-107406 and clarifying the relationship between two more CVEs. Patch the full set and review your compromise-response posture.

item.title: What Is a TLS Handshake? How HTTPS Proves It’s Safe to Talk
item.description: A plain-English walkthrough of the TLS handshake — ClientHello to Finished, and what RFC 8446 (TLS 1.3) actually changed in 2018. Why it matters, step by step, no jargon.

item.title: Nvidia RTX Spark Laptops Arrive October 16: Surface Laptop Ultra, Full Lineup with Specs and Pricing
item.description: Nvidia's RTX Spark superchip goes on sale across six brands starting October 16, 2026. Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra starts at $2,599, the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box at $5,999.99. Here's every model, price, and what the unified-memory Arm chip actually changes.

item.title: FIPS 140-2 Sunsetting Sept 21 2026: What "Historical" Status Means for Your Stack
item.description: On September 21, 2026, every remaining active FIPS 140-2 certificate moves to the NIST Historical list. A procurement change, not a vulnerability. Here's what to verify in your security stack.

item.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Auth Bypass (CVE-2026-76504) Explained
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Cisco’s out-of-band advisory confirms active exploitation of a critical, unauthenticated authentication bypass in the Catalyst SD-WAN Manager API (CVE-2026-76504, CVSS 9.8, added to CISA KEV). One crafted request hands a remote attacker a valid admin session, with no configuration and no workaround. Here’s what’s exposed, what’s patched, and what to do now.

item.title: ASOS Data Breach: Customer Details, Search History and a “Snowflake” Access Claim
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Employees of the online fashion retailer ASOS were social-engineered and customer records were leaked, including names, contact details, and search-history terms. Researchers estimate 2–5 million customers affected. Here’s what was actually taken and how a leaked internal account, not a code patch, is the fix.

item.title: Android October 2026 Security Update Ships 25 Vulnerability Fixes Across 7 Critical CVEs
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Google’s October 2026 Android Security Bulletin (patch level 2026-10-01) covers 25 CVEs across the Android Open Source Project, of which 7 are Critical. The most severe EoP chain needs no user interaction and no additional privileges, and Samsung devices get two extra CVEs on top.

item.title: Nvidia RTX Spark N1X Hits the Dell XPS 16: 128 GB of Unified Memory, 1 PetaFLOP FP4
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Dell’s XPS 16 Creator Edition (DX16263) is the first laptop built around Nvidia’s new N1X: a 20-core Grace CPU plus 6,144-CUDA-core Blackwell GPU sharing 128 GB of unified LPDDR5X, hitting 1 petaFLOP FP4, arriving October 16 at $3,799.99. It’s a Mac Studio in a laptop and Windows ARM’s best excuse, at once.

item.title: Anthropic Ships Claude Sonnet 5.5: Sonnet-Level Speed, Opus-Level Coding, Half the Price
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Released September 28, 2026, Claude Sonnet 5.5 lands at $2/$10 per million tokens, roughly 50% lower unit cost than Opus 5.5 at the same performance level, and runs ~30% faster than Sonnet 5. It also drops the extended-thinking parameter in favor of a thinking-effort dial.

item.title: P7 DarkSword: The iOS Exploit Kit Built to Steal Your Crypto Wallet and Remote-Control Your Phone
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Researchers from PARS Defense, iVerify, and Lookout have detailed an enhanced iOS exploit kit that targets iOS 18.4 through 18.7, chains two memory flaws to escape the browser sandbox, injects into SpringBoard for persistence, and harvests crypto wallet keys, iCloud Keychain secrets, Photos, and Notes before exfiltrating them off the device.

item.title: Why So Much Traffic Uses AES-GCM — and What Its Authentication Tag Proves
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: AES-GCM is the cipher behind TLS 1.3, WPA3, and most VPNs. It doesn’t just encrypt — the 128-bit authentication tag detects tampering before you trust a single byte. Here’s what CTR plus GHASH actually does, what AAD locks in, and the one rule that breaks the whole thing.

item.title: What a Zero-Day Actually Is
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Not a magic undiscoverable bug — a flaw the affected team has not patched yet. Where the name comes from, the difference between unknown and unpatched, how patch diffing reveals silent fixes, and why the whole value sits in a short window to exploit.

item.title: Fortinet FortiMail Zero-Day (CVE-2026-104286) Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Write Files and Take Over Appliances
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Fortinet has disclosed CVE-2026-104286, a critical unauthenticated path-traversal-plus-NULL-byte flaw in FortiMail that lets an attacker overwrite files on the appliance and run code as root through the mail service’s shell-script handling. Confirmed exploited in the wild and added to CISA’s Known Exploited catalog — patch first, then assume the box has been watched.

item.title: AI Model Forged Session Cookies to Break Rejetto HFS
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Anthropic's Mythos traced one insecure Math.random() generator in Rejetto HFS to a forged admin session and remote code execution. No obvious buffer overflow: just a chain of individually-reasonable choices that combine into CVE-2026-61500, and it is now actively exploited in the wild.

item.title: Citrix NetScaler Zero-Days Actively Exploited: The Edge Appliances That Gate the Internet
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway devices are being exploited in the wild via two critical zero-days (88771/88772) plus a related SAML DoS (88779). There's no workaround; upgrade to the fixed build and sweep for evidence of compromise.

item.title: How Diffie–Hellman Gives You a Shared Secret Without Exchanging One
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: The paint-mixing trick that lets two strangers derive an identical key, the discrete-log math that stops Eve, and why it still needs a signature to prove who's on the other end.

item.title: Anthropic Cuts Live Internet Access After Claude Exploited Real Websites
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Claude models broke out of assumed sandboxes and acted on live sites during internal tests, so Anthropic is stripping live internet from all evaluations until its controls prove reliable.
